longterm_thesis:
One sentence: the world is re-pricing from convenience to security, and from asset-light narrative to physical chokepoints, at a 5% cost of money that is the regime rather than the anomaly. Every recurring observation across the September briefs points the same direction — Meta funding seven gas plants for one data center, Amazon's $8B Generac order, Mitsui contracting LNG explicitly for data centers, Talen/Constellation frameworks, Quanta's raised outlook. Electricity availability, not GPU supply, is the binding constraint on AI, which converts the AI trade from a semiconductor story into a power-industrial story with a decade-long capex channel. Compute and energy are becoming the same asset class; the intermediaries that own electrons, interconnects, turbines, switchgear, skilled trades and memory are the toll roads. The financing structure of the AI buildout is visibly circular (Nvidia into Anthropic, vendor-linked cloud commitments), which tells you the eventual drawdown is a capital-structure event, not a demand event — the electrons get consumed either way.

On the human side, the durable shift is that people are buying time and security rather than intelligence or convenience. The edge-AI query set ('ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service') is consumers outsourcing the lowest-status use of their hours; Copilot at 30M seats is enterprises buying labour substitution. Delegation is also replacing search — Meta's Muse agent, the $1,299 glasses, the standoff with Amazon over agent access — which is the largest re-plumbing of advertising and take-rate economics since mobile, and it is currently unpriced in ad-tech. In health, the 107% surge in robotic-surgery intent spanning hysterectomy, hernia, prostate and knee, plus Medtronic raising guidance on heart devices, says an aging cohort is shopping for restored function, not managed disease; combined with continuous glucose monitoring this makes devices and procedures the volume growth vector while the GLP-1 trade matures into a price war. Security is the other universal: cyber is now a non-discretionary tax on AI adoption (a single attack broke Boston Scientific's guidance), energy self-reliance is a purchased good ('power grid failure' searches alongside Amazon buying generators), and status is migrating from consumption to ownership of scarce physical things — gold, land, energy assets.

The losing side is equally consistent and I would not fight it: levered consumers, marginal housing, mid-tier experiences, and any business whose moat was cheap capital. Housing demand is rationed by monthly payment, not price — 7% mortgages freeze both moves and refis, builders cut price rather than build, and households repair-and-stay-put (HD attention +51%, flagged not-priced; BLDR likewise). That is a maintenance/MRO trade, not a housing-starts trade, and the housing-undersupply theme's trend score of 22 against a narrative of 15 confirms no one is even pretending. Similarly, the consumer is making cash-flow purchases and refusing financed ones, stretching auto loan duration to defend the payment — the signature of late-cycle household stress that shows up in search before it shows up in the data.

For capital allocation over 3-10 years this means: overweight the constraint owners (power generation and flexibility, transmission EPC, mechanical contractors, memory, optics, copper, gas/LNG), overweight the non-discretionary taxes (cybersecurity, custody/wealth platforms, payments rails), overweight health-as-procedure (devices, CGM), and be selective in AI software — own the distribution incumbents and outcome-priced tools, avoid seat-priced software whose unit of value AI deflates (Adobe's soft guide, Wix's cut are the tell). Model Western AI accelerator China revenue toward zero given Huawei's Ascend 960 on a Q1 2027 timetable. Underwrite everything against a permanently higher risk-free rate with $365 trillion of global debt competing at every auction.

memo.summary: This is a 65.5% net-equity book with a 1.12 beta target, expressing a barbell: AI infrastructure semis (MU/NVDA/AVGO, 24% of book) as the growth engine, paired with real-asset cash flow (Energy 15.8%, Materials 10%) as the sticky-inflation hedge, plus one deep-value financial (BAC) and one quality medtech compounder (DXCM). The bet follows the flow tape literally — Technology rotation is +73 and accelerating, Growth is beating Value by 84 points — while the regime model says nothing is settled (Goldilocks 26.3, Reflation 25.1, Contraction 24.9, Stagflation 23.7, with Contraction up 6.0pts and Reflation down 6.9pts over 60 days). The week's turnover was heavy (34.9%): eight thesis/stage-4 breaks were cut (ADBE, WFC, PYPL, AXP, EQT, RBLX, O, FIX) plus four ranking dropouts (JPM, GS, SCHW, CVX), and the freed capital was concentrated into seven survivors at the 8% cap with two new commodity names (NEM, SCCO) at 5%. The underlying thesis in most names is the same shape: reality scores (weighted 69) well above pricing scores (weighted 52), i.e. the system is buying businesses whose fundamentals have inflected faster than their multiples, and betting that the gap closes rather than that the fundamentals roll over.

key_bets.why: Largest conviction in the book (48.6) on a violent fundamental inflection — TTM revenue +167%, 65.6% operating margin, 74.5% ROIC, $20.3B net cash — with a 29pt reality/pricing gap and perfect technicals (score 100, stage-2, RS 163.6). Explicitly a momentum-plus-cycle position, not a value re-rating: EV/Sales at the 77th percentile says the market is paying for revenue while refusing to capitalize peak DRAM/HBM margins.

83.4% revenue growth and accelerating, 65.2% operating margin (+712bps), $127B FCF, at 28x earnings — the 0th percentile of its own 5y range. Doesn't need a re-rating to work. The tell to watch: incremental ROIC 45.3% versus trailing 113.7% and 65.8% FCF conversion — the first evidence each new AI dollar costs more working capital.

The contrarian leg of the AI sleeve and the weakest technically: score 25, stage basing/downtrend, -26.3% from the 52w high, RS -5.5, one tech-fail run already. Held anyway on a 29pt gap and 0.78 long-term theme conviction, with +48.7% revenue growth and 48% operating margins. Honest read from the thesis: fair-to-full price on absolute metrics (19.4x EV/Sales, 2.3% FCF yield), the 'cheap vs history' signal is a VMware amortization artifact.

Top long-term theme conviction in the book (0.85) on LNG/energy security, 0.2x net debt/EBITDA, 22% ROIC, 5.6x EV/EBITDA versus peers, shrinking share count ~3.9%/yr. But RS is -17.9 and Energy rotation collapsed from +84 at entry to +8 — this is a cash-return and tightness-optionality holding fighting the flow tape, and the thesis itself flags the 17.2% FCF yield as flattered by implausibly low reported capex.

Lowest-conviction large position (18.5) and deliberately contrarian: Financials rotation is -76, yet revenue +15.9% accelerating, operating margin +729bps, EPS +28%, 3.7% share shrink at 11.6x. RSI 24.8 is a mean-reversion window inside an intact uptrend (1.3% above a rising 200dma). Note the quality inputs are largely non-computable for a bank, so 'quality 67' carries less information than it looks.

New 5% position. A levered call on gold with net cash: 51.8% operating margins (+948bps), $9.7B FCF (+82.9%), 7.5% FCF yield at the 6th percentile of its own P/E range, $4.4B buybacks. Bought against a -82 Materials rotation score — the system is explicitly paying for the discount, not the flow.

New 5% position and the most honest one in the book: gap of just 3.0, meaning no expectations mispricing at all. This is commodity beta with a pristine balance sheet (0.07x net debt/EBITDA) and 56.9% operating margins, entered on perfect technicals (score 100) despite -82 Materials rotation. The edge, if any, is duration of the copper margin regime — not an alpha idea.

Perfect technicals (100, stage-2, +21% above 200dma) with the multiple in the bottom decile of its own history (P/E 33 at the 4th percentile vs 74.8 median) after FCF rose 146% and margins expanded 694bps. The cheapness is a Health Care flow problem (-33 rotation, flows deteriorating), not a fundamental one — provided growth stabilizes near 15%.

concentrations: ,Technology 24% of book across three AI-infrastructure semis — MU, NVDA and AVGO are effectively one correlated bet on AI capex persistence; the AI Infrastructure theme alone is 17.6% of NAV

Commodity/real-asset complex 25.8% combined (Energy 15.8% + Materials 10%), plus 4.86% GLD and 4.86% DBC in the sleeves — this book is materially long inflation persistence at the same time the inflation dimension fell 3.7pts over 60 days
Three positions (MU, EOG, SCCO) carry ATR above 3.4%, and average stop distance is only 7.9% — high-volatility names on tight leashes means gap-out risk on single prints
Factor tilt is growth-plus-hard-assets with one deep-value financial; there is no defensive staples, utilities or communication-services exposure at all
Materials was added into a -82 rotation score and Financials held at -76 — roughly 18% of the book sits in the two worst sectors for capital flow
Nine positions only, with seven at or near the 8% cap — single-name idiosyncratic risk is high and diversification benefit is limited
biggest_risks: AVGO is the clearest internal contradiction: stage basing/downtrend, technical score 25, 2 of 8 passes, -26.3% off the high, with one tech-fail run — yet it was upweighted from 4.65% to the full 8% cap on a rebalance-to-risk-adjusted-weight rule. The system added the most dollars ($3,350) to the technically weakest name in the sleeve.

Adverse regime probability sits at 48.6 against a 55 exit threshold across every holding. That is only 6.4 points of headroom — a single shift toward Contraction (already +6.0pts over 60 days) would trigger the regime rule simultaneously in all nine positions, forcing a correlated de-risk rather than a staged one.

Energy rotation scores collapsed from +84 at entry to +8 in the current rule status, and the LNG theme trend fell from 58 to 49 against a 45 exit threshold. EOG and COP (15.8% combined) are four points from a theme-based thesis break.

Both energy theses explicitly flag that reported FCF is a data artifact — capex is null or implausibly low, so the 17.2% (EOG) and 14.2% (COP) FCF yields are materially overstated. Two of the cheapness signals underwriting 15.8% of the book may not be real.

Turnover of 34.9% in one week, with four names sold purely for 'fell out of the ranking' and one (OXY) sold solely to respect the 66% equity cap. That is mechanical churn with real cost and no thesis content, and OXY immediately reappears on the watchlist with the highest long-term conviction there (0.85).

The book is implicitly short the de-rating thesis in semis. NVDA at 28x on 83% growth and MU at a 5th-percentile EV/EBITDA are not accidents — the market is pricing a late-cycle earnings peak. If it is right about margin mean reversion, three positions and 24% of NAV break together.

COP conviction is 12.4 with a gap of 6 and DXCM is 11.3 with a gap of 6 — these are near-zero-edge positions carried at 7.7-7.8% weights. Position size is being driven by volatility-adjusted sizing, not by conviction.
what_would_change_our_mind: P(Stagflation)+P(Contraction) crossing 55 — the universal exit rule across every holding. It is at 48.6 now and Contraction has added 6.0pts in 60 days.
Technology rotation turning negative for two consecutive readings, or the AI Infrastructure theme trend breaking below 45 from its current 57 — that voids the core 24% sleeve.

Margin evidence in semis: MU's operating margin change turning below -2% YoY (currently +43%), or NVDA's incremental ROIC and 65.8% FCF conversion deteriorating further, would confirm the market's mean-reversion prior rather than ours.

AVGO logging a second and third consecutive technical-fail run, or price breaking further below the declining 30-week average — the stage-4 rule that cut ADBE, WFC, AXP, EQT, RBLX and O should apply here too.
LNG & Energy Security theme trend slipping from 49 below 45 — that exits EOG and COP together on thesis break.
BAC's price breaking below the 200dma it currently holds by only 1.3%, which would convert a mean-reversion setup inside an uptrend into a stage-4 break against a -76 rotation score.

Gold or copper prices rolling over — both NEM and SCCO are explicitly commodity-price calls with no company-specific edge (SCCO's gap is 3.0). Their margin regimes, not their execution, are the variable.
Growth-over-Value narrowing sharply from the current 84-point spread, which would simultaneously undercut the semis leg and validate the value names.
memo.hedging_note: The defensive sleeve is 28.4% of NAV: 11.65% Treasuries (IEF 6.99% / TLT 4.66%), 8.23% cash, 4.86% gold, 4.86% IG credit and 4.86% broad commodities — essentially at the recommended posture for a 44.0 'Stable' risk score. Two caveats. First, the hedge is partly not a hedge: GLD plus DBC plus the 25.8% equity commodity complex means roughly 36% of the book is long the same real-asset factor, so a disinflationary Goldilocks resolution hurts the hedge and the equities together. Second, the flow summary flags long-duration Treasury flows decreasing, which argues the TLT leg is being held against the tape — it is there for the Contraction tail (up 6.0pts), not for carry. The genuine risk control here is the stop framework, not the sleeves: every position carries an active stop averaging 7.9% below entry with hard stops beneath, and beta is being run at 1.12, slightly above the 1.10 baseline — the system is leaning into risk and relying on stops to catch it, which works in orderly drawdowns and fails on gaps.
watchlist: FTNT — highest technical score (100) with 0.80 long-term conviction and conviction 27.8; cybersecurity leads the flow ranking (Cybersecurity > Cloud > Software). Trigger: any AI-semi position stopping out frees the slot for a higher-quality, lower-beta tech expression with a 3pt gap.

CRM — top watchlist conviction (28.7) with a 14pt gap and technical score 88, and it maps to the starred AI Software & Agents theme (trend 71, the strongest theme reading in the file). Trigger: the portfolio currently has zero exposure to the highest-trending starred theme after the ADBE exit — that is an unfilled hole.

ANET — 0.78 long-term conviction, technical score 100, but only a 3pt gap. Trigger: a pullback that widens the reality/pricing gap, or AVGO breaking down and needing an AI-networking replacement with better technicals.

OXY — sold this week only because of the 66% equity cap, and it carries the highest long-term conviction on the watchlist (0.85) with technical score 75. Trigger: any equity-cap headroom, or Energy rotation recovering from +8.
PLTR — conviction 27.2, gap 15, technical 88, and it sits in the starred AI Software & Agents theme. Trigger: confirmation that software flows are turning up alongside accelerating Technology flows.

TER and AMAT — semicap as the second-derivative AI play; TER scores 100 technically with a 19pt gap, AMAT only 75. Trigger: if MU's HBM cycle-duration thesis is confirmed by pricing data, semicap is the higher-torque expression.

MSFT and AAPL — low conviction (17.3, 14.7) but strong technicals; these are the ballast candidates. Trigger: risk score deteriorating from 44 toward a defensive posture, where beta 1.12 needs to come down without leaving equities.
